clue.text: Intimidate the scourge of water hemlock

parts.note: to intimidate someone is to cow them
a scourge, a curse or ruin, is a bane

explanation.surface: Bullying the menace that is a poisonous plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant-name equivalence: the poisonous Cicuta of wet ground goes by both names and is fatal to grazing cattle.

clue.text: Game for a type of French toasted sandwich? Non, monsieur, has the last fragment

indicators.note: Non, monsieur tells the solver the sandwich goes without its monsieur

parts.words: a type of French toasted sandwich
parts.note: the croque-monsieur is the French toasted ham-and-cheese sandwich
taken as written

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word fragment

explanation.surface: A French waiter refusing a toasted sandwich and offering the last scrap instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Non' cancels the monsieur of the sandwich's name, leaving its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn game in which players knock wooden balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Verge on a method to agree

parts.note: a method is a way of doing something
to side with someone is to agree with them

explanation.surface: Coming close to finding a way to reach agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verge on' looks like a phrase meaning approach, but 'Verge' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassy edge beside a road, called the verge in Britain.

clue.text: Like to fold a tree

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
a pen is an enclosure for animals, like a sheep fold

explanation.surface: Fancying folding a tree, as one might origami.
explanation.definitionFit: A poplar whose leaves tremble in the slightest breeze.

clue.text: Hi, curates are upset with the holy sacrament

indicators.note: are upset means knocked over, so the letters of Hi, curates are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Clergy greeted cheerfully then left upset by the communion service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian rite of bread and wine, also called Holy Communion.

clue.text: Casting place discovered in front of railway termini

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: discovered means found

indicators.note: termini are the end stations, so the first and last letters of the word railway are taken

explanation.surface: A metalworks turned up beside the stations at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A works where molten metal is poured into moulds, the place where castings are made.

clue.text: Dress smeared with a stick of rock from Blackpool

indicators.note: with here means carried within, so the letters run inside the words of rock

explanation.surface: A dress smeared with sticky seaside candy from a Lancashire resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool rock is a stick of candy with letters running through it, a nod to the word running through 'of rock'; 'smeared', 'a stick' and 'from Blackpool' dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock is a woman's or girl's dress.

clue.text: The object of which is getting an empty case

definitions.text: The object of which is getting an empty case

parts.words: The object of which is getting an empty case
parts.note: the goal of an activity is a suitcase left with nothing in it, which happens when its contents are taken out after a trip

explanation.definitionFit: Taking clothes and belongings out of a suitcase or box after travel or a move.

clue.text: Order with a fly name

parts.note: Order is the taxonomic rank; one insect order takes its name from the two wings of flies

explanation.definitionFit: The insect order of two-winged true flies, including houseflies and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Charge for using enclosure three foot ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece above the second in this down answer

parts.note: three feet make a yard
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fee for a pen for animals, set three feet in front of the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee paid for keeping livestock in a stockyard, or for the use of a yard.

clue.text: I comply to order of athletic games

indicators.note: to order means to arrange, so the letters of I comply are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An athlete obediently following instructions at the games.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for the four-yearly international sporting festival, the greatest athletics meeting.

clue.text: In theory no upsetting a daily

indicators.note: upsetting tips the word no over so that it reads backwards

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Saying no to a newspaper, in principle at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for what holds in principle, as written down, though perhaps not in practice.

clue.text: Give marriage a lift, it's up the pole

parts.note: a marriage is a union
to jack something is to lift it, as with a car jack

explanation.surface: A cheerful nudge to a wedding, with a flag flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national flag, which is hoisted up a flagpole.

clue.text: Coach ends knocking ale back with crab's claw

indicators.note: the ends of the word Coach are its first and last letters
back says the word ale is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: A coach party knocking back beer with a crab dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking ale back' reads as drinking; 'knocking' only completes that phrase, while 'back' turns ALE into ELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoological term for the pincer of a crustacean or scorpion.

clue.text: In that place its three fold

indicators.note: fold here means crumple, so the letters of three are folded into a new order

explanation.surface: Something folded in three parts, somewhere over yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb of location, pointing to a spot away from the speaker.

clue.text: Calculate and scour out wrong counter-measure

indicators.note: scour is taken out and the remaining letters of counter-measure are arranged wrong, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Work it out, and wipe away the mistaken response to a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, C, O, U, R out of COUNTERMEASURE and rearrange the nine letters that are left.
explanation.definitionFit: To count off items one by one, listing or reckoning them.

clue.text: I'm to whip in the cheese to make it overlap

parts.note: I'm is written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: in puts the whip inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a cat is a whip, as in the cat-o'-nine-tails

explanation.surface: A cook whisking something into soft cheese so the slices lie in layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make it' is padding: the pieces make the word meaning overlap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie layered like roof tiles or fish scales, each edge covering the next.

clue.text: Stop hymn of Spain being Venetian boating song

parts.note: a bar is a barrier that stops passage
a carol is a Christmas hymn
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Halting a Spanish hymn in favour of a gondolier's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier's song with a rocking rhythm, or music imitating one.

clue.text: "Ss doubter" refurbished for the American farmer

indicators.note: refurbished means done up afresh, so the letters of Ss doubter are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A sceptic made over into a farmer in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: US slang for a prairie farmer who broke up the turf to plough it.

clue.text: Set with FBI's tranche

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the word set contains the agents

parts.note: taken as written
the FBI's agents are G-men, government men

explanation.surface: A group put together with a slice of federal agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice of something larger.

clue.text: Doubtful name for debts

parts.note: to dub is to give a name
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: An uncertain label for what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain, open to question, not to be relied on.

clue.text: Gawped — even when wicket was lost

definitions.text: Gawped — even when wicket was lost

indicators.note: was lost says the wicket goes missing from the word Gawped

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A spectator staring open-mouthed even as a batsman was dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gawp and gape mean the same, so taking W out of the first spelling still leaves a word for staring.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp and to gape both mean to stare open-mouthed, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Prince is at the age for a lad to have a girl's hairstyle

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young prince old enough to wear a girlish haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob with the ends turned under, named after a medieval page's haircut.

clue.text: The dun turned up indeed stripped

annotationWithheld.why: The dun turned up indeed stripped: NUD (dun turned up) goes inside DEED, but the single word 'indeed' must give both the container signal 'in' and the letters DEED, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: The dun turned up indeed stripped

clue.text: Portrayed butler as having gone with the wind round Birkenhead!

definitions.text: Portrayed butler as having gone with the wind round Birkenhead

indicators.note: round says the wind wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
read as Birken-head, the head of the word is its first letter, B; Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside

explanation.surface: Someone who played a butler blown away by the wind on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable played Rhett Butler in the 1939 film Gone with the Wind; 'butler' is the character's surname, not a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark, the Hollywood star who played Rhett Butler in the 1939 film epic.

clue.text: Game bird extremely piquant, a margin for improvement

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word piquant
for improvement means the letters of a margin are reworked into a better order

explanation.surface: A spicy game dish that still leaves room to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse of mountains and tundra, shot for sport, that turns white in winter.

clue.text: They have plugs for smokers

parts.note: plugs are cakes of pressed tobacco, and the bowls that take such tobacco are lit by smokers

explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco holders: a bowl on a stem, packed and lit by smokers.

clue.text: Sadly deems such rewards

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters of deems are jumbled

explanation.surface: Regrettably someone judges these to be prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or poetic word for a deserved reward or recompense.

clue.text: Skin old duck and moan at fish

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
to carp is to moan or complain

explanation.surface: Peeling an aged duck and grumbling over the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at fish' rounds off the surface and hints that carp is also a fish; the wordplay needs only 'moan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term for the outer layer of a fruit's wall, its peel or rind.

clue.text: On offer, but just too much

definitions.text: On offer, but just too much

parts.words: On offer, but just too much
parts.note: describes a bid at an auction or the bridge table that goes a little beyond what is sensible

explanation.definitionFit: To bid more than something is worth, or more than one's hand justifies in bridge.

clue.text: Food samplers first try Michaelmas daisies

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word try

parts.note: Michaelmas daisies are asters, which flower around Michaelmas (29 September)

explanation.surface: Diners invited to have a go at autumn flowers before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: People employed to try dishes or wines and judge their quality.

clue.text: Sad eyes show how one tried

indicators.note: show here means put on display afresh, so the letters of Sad eyes are shown in a new order

explanation.surface: Mournful eyes reveal how hard someone tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how one' is linking padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned verb: to essay something is to attempt it.
